title: The specification's availability model is replaced: no clock intervals per weekday, no per-interval pause budget, no `unavailable` against `replace_intervals` exceptions
No 90-day horizon with a 7-to-365 setting, and no capacity override
What stands in its place is a weekly minute budget, a session per working day, per-date entries, and a monthly account
A weekday holds its net work minutes and nothing else: one window, no clock times, no pause budget
One configured planned start supplies the clock for future days, and the observed start replaces it the moment the day begins
A day's window is its start, plus its minutes, plus the break reserve
Zero minutes is a non-working day
Whole minutes throughout
One record per date: the start, the leave time, the break reserve
The leave is derived as start plus minutes plus reserve unless the user states one
"stay later today" or "I must leave earlier" are simply statements that move the leave, at any moment of the day
A day with planned work that has not been started is not a session
The session ends when the user says it ends
A day left unended gets an inferred end: the end of the last task time entry logged that day, or, when nothing was logged, the start plus the day's target plus the reserve, so the day is never...
Either way a persistent notice asks for a real end per unfinished day
The session takes the place of §5.17's capacity override, so the overridable rules fall from three to two
Time off, two kinds on one record: a date, a minute count, a kind
`vacation` replaces both the day's capacity and the month's target, and cannot exceed the weekday's minutes
`flex` replaces only the day's capacity and may be more, fewer, or zero minutes
The month's total never grows; only vacation reduces it
Entries may be recorded on past dates, and the review shows the conflict when presence or logged task time disagrees with one
The target is the month's weekday minutes minus vacation
Worked is presence: the session's window minus its reserve, deliberately not task time
The balance is worked minus target inside the running month
A permitted shortfall and permitted surplus, each a minute count or unlimited, clamp what a month may end at
A target shortfall and target surplus, which the plan reconciles to, catching up to the band's edge and stopping there
A target may not exceed its allowance unless that allowance is unlimited
The gap between the balance and the target band is settled in thirty-minute increments over the days after today that have work scheduled, in date order, cycling from the first day while the...
A day carrying minutes of its own is never modified
That invariant binds every future projection algorithm, not only this one
The algorithm is a configuration point with one implementation in v1
A deadline is a date or an instant, a sealed pair rather than one nullable timestamp
A date means before that local day ends
An instant is accepted only for the current local day, so 15:00 on a task due tomorrow is rejected rather than rounded
The rule is input validation, not a stored constraint, so an instant that later passes simply stays past
Project deadlines follow it too, and every effective-deadline comparison reads a date as the end of its day
This refines the deadline that `task-model-comparison` recorded as one optional instant
It is bounded by the day's capacity, so with three hours left it holds three hours
It is not re-planned as time passes; the plan stays and a cut line moves up it, showing which planned items now fall past the leave
It re-plans on a data change or at the next day, never on the clock
The fit signal is one line plus that cut: planned minutes, available minutes, and what no longer fits
Notices: one concept for everything the system says
A notice has a persistence flag, on while its condition holds and off for a one-off that stays until dismissed; a level of `info` or `warning`; an optional entity reference; a message; and a flag...
The list and the dismissal live on `ForPlanningQueries`, which makes that port a query with an acknowledgement rather than adding a ninth port
The OS copy is informative only and delivered once; if the user interacts with it there, the interaction is discarded
Nine notice types: `deadline_tight` (warning), `deadline_missed` (warning), `estimate_overrun` (info), `blocked_deadline_path` (warning), `dependency_cycle_prevented` (info)
`no_timetable` (warning, renamed from `no_working_hours`), `horizon_over_capacity` (info, renamed from `plan_over_capacity`), `month_will_not_settle` (warning, new), ...
`missing_session_end` (warning, new, one per unfinished day)
The specification's `critical` severity retires; errors are handled before they could become notices
The review: the month is the unit. Each past day shows its target minutes, its presence minutes, and the difference, with the month's balance as the headline
A day carrying vacation or flex shows the conflict when logged work disagrees with it, and time off recorded late is visible
Task time is not the compared quantity
Concrete allocation covers fourteen days
A projection continues past it by repeating the weekday pattern and following the month's balance, marked as a projection and as rough beyond four weeks
`horizon_over_capacity` carries the meaning "you are using this tool beyond its design": a backlog that fills more than the fourteen days is discouraged rather than refused
Deadlines six weeks out are ordinary; a three-hour task planned two weeks out is the case that should feel wrong
`architecture`: `ForDefiningCapacity` owns the timetable, the per-date entries, and the four balancing settings; `ForTrackingTime` owns sessions
`ForPlanningQueries` gains the notice list and dismissal
`ForPlanning` receives day capacities and the month's balance as data, not a store
`task-model-comparison`: its deadline field is refined to the sealed date-or-instant pair
`decisions-estimates-time`: task time entries serve remaining effort and per-task accounting only, never the month's account
`decisions-forecast-warnings`: the notice model, the nine types and their levels, the retirement of `critical`, and the confidence labels on projections beyond the horizon
`decisions-data-lifecycle`: removal of per-date entries and of notices, and the inferred session end as a provisional value that a correction overwrites
`decisions-agent-interface`: agents read notices, dismiss a one-off only on explicit request, and treat a leave time as a scheduling input
`child-efforts`: the setup journey has to ask for the weekly minutes, the planned start, the break reserve, and the balancing settings
`child-efforts`: the review surface compares presence, not task time
